Abstract
This study empirically examines how organizational and perceptual factors influence organizational creativity through change acceptance in the context of artificial intelligence (Al) adoption in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Conceptualizing Al adoption as an organizational change, this research focuses on employees’ perceptions, organizational culture, and the process of change acceptance, rather than solely on technological or structural factors. The results indicate that organizational support and knowledge-sharing culture have significant positive effects on change acceptance, whereas perceived risk and performance expectancy do not. Moreover, both change acceptance and knowledge-sharing culture positively affect organizational creativity, and organizational support and knowledge-sharing culture indirectly influence organizational creativity through change acceptance. These findings suggest that Al utilization outcomes in SMEs depend more on organizational support, cultural conditions, and employees’ acceptance of change than on technological factors alone, thereby extending Al adoption research toward an organizational behavior and change management perspective.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content:
This study empirically examines how organizational and perceptual factors influence organizational creativity through change acceptance in the context of artificial intelligence (Al) adoption in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Conceptualizing Al adoption as an organizational change, this research focuses on employees’ perceptions, organizational culture, and the process of change acceptance, rather than solely on technological or structural factors. The results indicate that organizational support and knowledge-sharing culture have significant positive effects on change acceptance, whereas perceived risk and performance expectancy do not. Moreover, both change acceptance and knowledge-sharing culture positively affect organizational creativity, and organizational support and knowledge-sharing culture indirectly influence organizational creativity through change acceptance. These findings suggest that Al utilization outcomes in SMEs depend more on organizational support, cultural conditions, and employees’ acceptance of change than on technological factors alone, thereby extending Al adoption research toward an organizational behavior and change management perspective.
